groups.title: A garden on campus
groups.passage: A small garden behind the campus library used to be an empty parking area. Last spring, a group of students planted vegetables there. They chose plants that needed little water because the area receives limited rain. The students now meet every Sunday morning to care for the garden. Some of the vegetables go to the campus kitchen, and the rest are shared among volunteers. The project has also created a quiet place where students can take a break between classes.

questions.prompt: Why did the students choose plants that needed little water?

options.text: The campus kitchen requested those plants.
There is limited rain in the area.
The students only visited once a month.
The garden had too much shade.

questions.explanation: The passage directly links the choice of plants to limited rainfall.
questions.source: scripts/make-examples.mjs · 本项目自编演示 · q1

questions.prompt: Which activity is NOT mentioned as a use of the garden?

options.text: Growing vegetables for the campus kitchen.
Providing a place to rest between classes.

questions.explanation: Music performances are not mentioned in the passage.

questions.prompt:
Your professor is teaching a class about university life. Write a post responding to the professor. State your view and support it with a specific reason or example. You may acknowledge a useful feature of the other option.
Professor: Should universities spend more money on quiet individual study rooms or on shared group spaces?
Maya: I would choose more quiet rooms. When I read a difficult chapter, nearby conversations make it hard to follow the argument.
Jordan: I would choose shared spaces. My group often needs a place to compare notes and explain problems to one another.
